Build a season calendar

Source: R/creel-calendar.R
creel_calendar.Rd

creel_calendar() returns every day of the season, one row per date, with its day type and stratum: the calendar creel_design() takes. Unsampled days must be in the calendar, because they are the population days the totals expand to, and each date must appear once.

Usage

creel_calendar(
  start,
  end,
  strata = c("month", "day_type"),
  weekend_days = NULL,
  holidays = NULL,
  special_periods = NULL,
  season_blocks = NULL
)

Arguments

start, end

First and last day of the season, as a Date or "YYYY-MM-DD".

strata

Character vector: the parts of the stratum label, any of "season_block", "month", "week" and "day_type", in the order they appear in the label.

weekend_days

Day names (full or three-letter English, any case) that form the weekend. NULL (default) means Saturday and Sunday. The weekend days must be consecutive, because the week starts after them.

holidays

Optional Date vector (or "YYYY-MM-DD" strings) of days treated as weekend days.

special_periods

Optional data frame of periods that are strata of their own: start_date, end_date and label, with an optional reason, as generate_schedule() takes. Periods with different labels cannot overlap.

season_blocks

Optional data frame with start_date and label. Each row starts a block that runs until the next row's start_date; the first must be the season's first day. Required when strata includes "season_block", and refused otherwise.

Value

A data frame with one row per day of the season: date, month (integer), week (integer, week of the season), day_type ("weekday", "weekend" or "special"), season_block (when season_blocks is supplied) and stratum.

Strata

strata names the parts the stratum label is built from, in order:

  • "season_block": the block's label from season_blocks;

  • "month": the month, as "06";

  • "week": the week of the season, as "wk01". Week 1 starts on the season's first day, and each later week starts on the day after the last weekend day (Monday when the weekend is Saturday and Sunday), so a weekend is never split between two weeks. The first and last weeks can be partial;

  • "day_type": "weekday" or "weekend".

The default, c("month", "day_type"), gives labels such as "06_weekend".

Holidays and special periods

A date in holidays is a weekend day of its stratum: its day_type is "weekend", and a holiday Monday in June falls in "06_weekend". It does not move week boundaries: a holiday Monday is in the week it starts.

A date in special_periods is a stratum of its own: its day_type is "special" and its stratum is the period's label, whatever strata says. A period is not split by month, week or block, so a holiday weekend running from 30 June to 2 July is one stratum. (Apportioning such a stratum's total back to months is #429.) A date that is both a holiday and in a special period is in the special period.

Holidays and special periods are dates, not rules: the package does not know which holidays an agency observes or how it blocks them.

A holiday or special period outside the season is refused, not dropped: it usually means the wrong year.

See also

Other "Scheduling": attach_count_times(), daylight_shifts(), generate_bus_schedule(), generate_count_times(), generate_progressive_start(), generate_schedule(), new_creel_schedule(), read_schedule(), validate_creel_schedule(), write_schedule()

Examples

cal <- creel_calendar(
  "2024-05-01", "2024-09-02",
  holidays = as.Date(c("2024-05-27", "2024-09-02")),
  special_periods = data.frame(
    start_date = "2024-07-04", end_date = "2024-07-07",
    label = "july4"
  )
)
table(cal$stratum)
#> 
#> 05_weekday 05_weekend 06_weekday 06_weekend 07_weekday 07_weekend 08_weekday 
#>         22          9         20         10         21          6         22 
#> 08_weekend 09_weekend      july4 
#>          9          2          4 

creel_design(cal, date = date, strata = stratum)

# Early and late season blocks, by day type
creel_calendar(
  "2024-05-01", "2024-08-31",
  strata = c("season_block", "day_type"),
  season_blocks = data.frame(
    start_date = c("2024-05-01", "2024-07-01"),
    label = c("early", "late")
  )
) |> head()
#>         date month week day_type season_block       stratum
#> 1 2024-05-01     5    1  weekday        early early_weekday
#> 2 2024-05-02     5    1  weekday        early early_weekday
#> 3 2024-05-03     5    1  weekday        early early_weekday
#> 4 2024-05-04     5    1  weekend        early early_weekend
#> 5 2024-05-05     5    1  weekend        early early_weekend
#> 6 2024-05-06     5    2  weekday        early early_weekday
